title: En detrimento de: quién o qué sale perjudicado

sections.content: En detrimento de (to the detriment of) names who or what suffers as a result of a decision that benefits something else -- useful for describing policy trade-offs where one priority is favored at another's expense. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Los recortes al gasto público, en detrimento sobre todo de la salud y la educación, se combinaron con una inflación descontrolada.
items.english: Cuts to public spending, to the detriment especially of health and education, combined with uncontrolled inflation.

items.spanish: El aumento del precio del transporte fue impuesto en detrimento de los sectores más pobres de la población.
items.english: The transport price increase was imposed to the detriment of the poorest sectors of the population.

items.spanish: Muchos gobiernos priorizaron la estabilidad macroeconómica en detrimento del bienestar inmediato de sus propios ciudadanos.
items.english: Many governments prioritized macroeconomic stability to the detriment of their own citizens' immediate well-being.

items.spanish: El crecimiento del sector informal se produjo, en gran medida, en detrimento de la calidad y estabilidad del empleo.
items.english: The growth of the informal sector happened, to a large extent, to the detriment of employment quality and stability.

sections.content: En detrimento de always names the loser in a trade-off -- pair it naturally with a phrase describing who benefits (a favor de or en beneficio de) when a reading wants to make the full trade-off explicit.
